claim: The gltA gene encodes citrate synthase (CS) in E. coli.
source: We discovered that key mutations in the gltA gene, which encodes citrate synthase (CS), occurred both before and after Escherichia coli gained the ability to grow aerobically on citrate (Cit+ phenotype) during the Lenski long-term evolution experiment.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established scientific knowledge about the gltA gene function.

claim: Key mutations in the gltA gene occurred both before and after E. coli gained the ability to grow aerobically on citrate during the Lenski LTEE.
source: We discovered that key mutations in the gltA gene, which encodes citrate synthase (CS), occurred both before and after Escherichia coli gained the ability to grow aerobically on citrate (Cit+ phenotype) during the Lenski long-term evolution experiment.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The first gltA mutation (gltA1) increases CS activity by disrupting NADH-inhibition of the enzyme.
source: The first gltA mutation, which increases CS activity by disrupting NADH-inhibition of this enzyme, is beneficial for growth on the acetate and contributed to preserving the rudimentary Cit+ trait from extinction when it first evolved.
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements of NADH binding and inhibition kinetics presented in the study.

claim: The gltA1 mutation is beneficial for growth on acetate.
source: The first gltA mutation, which increases CS activity by disrupting NADH-inhibition of this enzyme, is beneficial for growth on the acetate and contributed to preserving the rudimentary Cit+ trait from extinction when it first evolved.
evidence: This is supported by fitness assays and growth curves in acetate-supplemented media.

claim: The gltA1 mutation contributed to preserving the rudimentary Cit+ trait from extinction when it first evolved.
source: The first gltA mutation, which increases CS activity by disrupting NADH-inhibition of this enzyme, is beneficial for growth on the acetate and contributed to preserving the rudimentary Cit+ trait from extinction when it first evolved.
evidence: This is inferred from fitness experiments showing epistatic interactions between gltA1 and citT mutations.

claim: A second wave of beneficial gltA mutations (gltA2) evolved that reduced CS activity to below the ancestral level.
source: A second wave of beneficial gltA mutations then evolved that reduced CS activity to below the ancestral level.
evidence: This is supported by enzyme kinetics measurements and mRNA expression data for gltA2 variants.

claim: The Lenski LTEE with E. coli has spanned more than 25 years of microbial adaptation.
source: The Lenski long-term evolution experiment (LTEE) with E. coli provides a unique opportunity to study how metabolic and regulatory networks have changed over a history spanning more than 25 years of microbial adaptation (Lenski and Travisano, 1994; Lenski et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original LTEE publications.

claim: Cells in one of the twelve LTEE populations evolved aerobic citrate utilization (Cit+ phenotype).
source: In particular, cells in one of the twelve LTEE populations evolved a qualitatively new metabolic capability—aerobic citrate utilization (Cit+ phenotype)—that enabled them to colonize a previously unoccupied ecological niche (Blount et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work documenting the Cit+ evolution.

claim: The Cit+ innovation enabled E. coli to colonize a previously unoccupied ecological niche.
source: In particular, cells in one of the twelve LTEE populations evolved a qualitatively new metabolic capability—aerobic citrate utilization (Cit+ phenotype)—that enabled them to colonize a previously unoccupied ecological niche (Blount et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation and is inferred from the fact that citrate was abundant but unused before the innovation.

claim: The Cit+ innovation is highly beneficial because it grants access to an abundant and previously untapped nutrient.
source: This Cit+ innovation is highly beneficial because it grants access to an abundant and previously untapped nutrient.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental design of the LTEE and the observed population dynamics after Cit+ evolved.

claim: A Cit+ variant has evolved in just one of the twelve LTEE populations.
source: So far, a Cit+ variant has evolved in just one of the twelve LTEE populations, and then only after ∼15 years of evolution.
evidence: This is an observation from the LTEE documented in previous publications.

claim: The Cit+ variant evolved only after approximately 15 years of evolution.
source: So far, a Cit+ variant has evolved in just one of the twelve LTEE populations, and then only after ∼15 years of evolution.
evidence: This is an observation from the LTEE timeline.

claim: The rarity of the Cit+ innovation suggests that accessing this new metabolic trait is contingent on a multi-step mutational pathway.
source: The rarity of the Cit+ innovation suggests that accessing this new metabolic trait is contingent on a multi-step mutational pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Cit+ evolved only once despite twelve replicate populations.

claim: The evolution of aerobic citrate utilization in the LTEE involved three stages: potentiation, actualization, and refinement.
source: The evolution of aerobic citrate utilization in the LTEE involved three stages: potentiation, actualization, and refinement.
evidence: This is a conceptual framework supported by previous work and the data in this study.

claim: Actualization of Cit+ was caused by a duplication that activated expression of the citT citrate:succinate antiporter gene through promoter capture.
source: This transition was caused by a duplication that activated expression of the citT citrate:succinate antiporter gene through promoter capture (Blount et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work that characterized the citT mutation.

claim: The citT mutation on its own confers only extremely weak citrate utilization.
source: However, on its own this mutation confers only extremely weak citrate utilization.
evidence: This is supported by growth experiments with strains containing only the citT mutation.

claim: The rudimentary Cit+ trait was refined to a stronger phenotype (Cit++) when cells capable of fully exploiting citrate during each 24 hr growth cycle evolved.
source: Subsequently, this rudimentary Cit+ trait was refined to a stronger phenotype, Cit++ , when cells that were capable of fully exploiting citrate during each 24 hr growth cycle evolved, coincident with a large increase in cell density in this LTEE population (Blount et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work documenting the population dynamics.

claim: The evolution of Cit++ was coincident with a large increase in cell density in the LTEE population.
source: Subsequently, this rudimentary Cit+ trait was refined to a stronger phenotype, Cit++ , when cells that were capable of fully exploiting citrate during each 24 hr growth cycle evolved, coincident with a large increase in cell density in this LTEE population (Blount et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an observation from the LTEE documented in previous work.

claim: A promoter mutation that activated expression of the dctA C4-dicarboxylate:H+ symporter gene was a chief refining mutation for Cit++.
source: Chief among the refining mutations was a promoter mutation that activated expression of the dctA C4-dicarboxylate:H+ symporter gene (Quandt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Rudimentary citrate utilization via activation of the citT gene would have been at a selective disadvantage if it appeared in a non-potentiated genetic background.
source: However, this simple two-step mutational pathway was apparently inaccessible without the prior evolution of one or more unknown mutations that created a potentiated genetic background (Blount et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from previous work and supported by the fitness experiments in this study.

claim: The gltA gene was mutated twice in most Cit++ isolates, once before and once after Cit+ evolved.
source: Multiple mutations in one gene are rare in LTEE lineages that have retained the low ancestral mutation rate (Barrick et al., 2009; Wielgoss et al., 2011), yet the gltA gene was mutated twice in most Cit++ isolates, once before and once after Cit+ evolved.
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing data from LTEE isolates.

claim: Multiple mutations in one gene are rare in LTEE lineages that have retained the low ancestral mutation rate.
source: Multiple mutations in one gene are rare in LTEE lineages that have retained the low ancestral mutation rate (Barrick et al., 2009; Wielgoss et al., 2011), yet the gltA gene was mutated twice in most Cit++ isolates, once before and once after Cit+ evolved.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous genomic analyses of LTEE populations.

claim: The gltA1 allele is a single base change that causes an A258T amino acid substitution in citrate synthase.
source: The earliest evolved allele (gltA1) is a single base change that causes an amino acid substitution (A258T) in this enzyme (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing data and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was present in every Cit+ strain sequenced.
source: This mutation was present in every Cit+ strain and in earlier Cit– clones from the clade that gave rise to Cit+.
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing of multiple LTEE isolates.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was present in earlier Cit– clones from the clade that gave rise to Cit+.
source: This mutation was present in every Cit+ strain and in earlier Cit– clones from the clade that gave rise to Cit+.
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The gltA1 mutation arose before the Cit+ phenotype evolved.
source: Therefore, the gltA1 mutation arose before the Cit+ phenotype evolved.
evidence: This is inferred from the presence of gltA1 in Cit– clones ancestral to Cit+ strains.

claim: Three secondary gltA mutations (gltA2 alleles) were found separately in the genomes of different Cit+ clones.
source: Three secondary gltA mutations (gltA2 alleles) were also found, separately, in the genomes of different Cit+ clones (gltA2-4, gltA2-6, or gltA2-7).
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing data from multiple Cit+ isolates.

claim: Each gltA2 base substitution causes an additional single amino acid change in the citrate synthase protein sequence.
source: Each of these base substitutions causes an additional single amino acid change in the citrate synthase protein sequence (A124T, V152A, or A162V, respectively).
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing and translation of the DNA sequences.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was first detected at 25,000 generations in metagenomic sequencing.
source: The earliest we detected the gltA1 mutation was at 25,000 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing of archived LTEE population samples.

claim: The gltA1 allele dropped to a frequency below detection (∼1–5%) at 30,000 generations.
source: Curiously, this allele dropped to a frequency within the population below the level of detection (∼1–5%) in the next sample analyzed at 30,000 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing data showing allele frequencies over time.

claim: The gltA1 allele emerged again at 33,000 generations and reached nearly 100% frequency by 33,500 generations.
source: The gltA1 allele emerged again at 33,000 generations and reached nearly 100% frequency in the population by 33,500 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing tracking allele frequencies.

claim: The resurgence of gltA1 coincided with the rise of the Cit++ subpopulation containing citT and dctA* mutations.
source: This resurgence coincided with the rise of the newly evolved gltA1-containing Cit++ subpopulation that had also accumulated the citT and dctA* mutations necessary for robust citrate utilization by this time (Quandt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing and previous characterization of the mutations.

claim: The clade that gave rise to Cit+ was rare within the population for several thousand generations prior to the evolution and refinement of Cit++.
source: These gltA1 allele dynamics suggest that the clade that gave rise to Cit+ was rare within the population for several thousand generations prior to the evolution and refinement of this metabolic innovation that enabled it to achieve numerical dominance.
evidence: This is inferred from the allele frequency dynamics observed in metagenomic sequencing.

claim: Two of the three gltA2 mutations found in sequenced clones and six other gltA2 mutations were present in ≥5% of the population at some point.
source: Two of the three gltA2 mutations found in the sequenced clones and six other gltA2 mutations were present in ≥5% of the population at some point.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing data tracking mutation frequencies.

claim: All additional gltA2 alleles detected are nonsynonymous mutations, except for one that is a single-base substitution 14 base pairs upstream of the gltA start codon.
source: All of these additional gltA2 alleles are also nonsynonymous mutations, except for one that is a single-base substitution 14 base pairs upstream of the gltA start codon.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the DNA sequences from metagenomic data.

claim: The first gltA2 mutation (gltA2-1) was detected at 33,000 generations.
source: The first gltA2 mutation (gltA2-1) was detected at 33,000 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing of population samples.

claim: The gltA2-1 mutation was completely displaced within approximately 1000 generations by competition with other genetically diverged subpopulations.
source: This mutation was apparently completely displaced within ∼1000 generations by competition with various other genetically diverged subpopulations, some of which had other gltA2 alleles.
evidence: This is based on tracking allele frequencies over time in metagenomic data.

claim: The gltA2-4 mutation had swept to fixation within the population by 38,000 generations.
source: By 38,000 generations, the gltA2-4 mutation had swept to fixation within the population, and no new gltA mutations were observed after 40,000 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing showing allele frequencies.

claim: No new gltA mutations were observed after 40,000 generations.
source: By 38,000 generations, the gltA2-4 mutation had swept to fixation within the population, and no new gltA mutations were observed after 40,000 generations.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing of later population samples.

claim: A de novo point mutation 182 base pairs upstream of the gltA start codon (gltA2-R allele) was found in every sequenced REGRES clone that retained the gltA1 mutation.
source: We found a de novo point mutation 182 base pairs upstream of the gltA start codon (gltA2-R allele) in every one of the sequenced REGRES clones that retained the gltA1 mutation present in the initial Cit++ clone (Quandt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing of REGRES-derived clones.

claim: A secondary gltA2 mutation was needed for robust citrate utilization under REGRES selection conditions.
source: These results suggest that a secondary gltA2 mutation was also needed for robust citrate utilization under these conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the consistent appearance of gltA2-R in all REGRES clones selected for citrate growth.

claim: Without the pCitT plasmid, cells containing the gltA1 mutation grew indistinguishably from EQ119 cells with a fully wild-type citrate synthase sequence.
source: Without the pCitT plasmid, and therefore without access to citrate, cells containing the gltA1 mutation grew indistinguishably from EQ119 cells with a fully wild-type citrate synthase sequence (gltAwt allele) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on growth curve measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cells with both the gltA1 and gltA2-R mutations had slower growth rates and reduced final cell densities compared to the strain with only the gltA1 mutation in Cit– background.
source: However, cells with both the gltA1 and gltA2-R mutations had somewhat slower growth rates and reduced final cell densities compared to the strain with only the gltA1 mutation, indicating that addition of the gltA2-R is deleterious when citrate cannot be used as a carbon and energy source.
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Addition of the gltA2-R mutation is deleterious when citrate cannot be used as a carbon and energy source.
source: However, cells with both the gltA1 and gltA2-R mutations had somewhat slower growth rates and reduced final cell densities compared to the strain with only the gltA1 mutation, indicating that addition of the gltA2-R is deleterious when citrate cannot be used as a carbon and energy source.
evidence: This is inferred from the growth curve data.

claim: In Cit++ cells, the gltA1 mutation was strongly deleterious, displaying both a longer lag phase and a slower exponential growth rate.
source: When made Cit++ via transformation with the pCitT plasmid, EQ119 cells with the gltA1 mutation grew noticeably worse than those with the gltAwt allele, displaying both a longer lag phase and a slower exponential growth rate (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on growth curve measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: Addition of the gltA2-R mutation in Cit++ context relieved the defect caused by gltA1 and resulted in improved growth compared to cells with wild-type citrate synthase.
source: Addition of the gltA2-R mutation in this context relieved the defect caused by gltA1 and even resulted in improved growth compared to cells with a wild-type citrate synthase sequence.
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The evolved gltA1 allele had no detectable effect on the fitness of strain ZDB478 in DM25.
source: In DM25, the evolved gltA1 allele had no detectable effect on the fitness of strain ZDB478, but it did improve the competitive fitness of strain ZDB483 by ∼3.5% (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on co-culture competition experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The evolved gltA1 allele improved the competitive fitness of strain ZDB483 by approximately 3.5% in DM25.
source: In DM25, the evolved gltA1 allele had no detectable effect on the fitness of strain ZDB478, but it did improve the competitive fitness of strain ZDB483 by ∼3.5% (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on co-culture competition experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The gltA1 mutation increased fitness in both ZDB478 and ZDB483 strains in DM25 medium supplemented with acetate.
source: We found that the gltA1 mutation increased fitness in both strains under these conditions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on competition assays in acetate-supplemented medium shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Other mutations present in evolved clones ZDB478 and ZDB483 are required for gltA1 to have beneficial effects on acetate utilization.
source: Other mutations present in these evolved clones are required for gltA1 to have these beneficial effects, as we found that adding gltA1 on its own to the ancestral REL606 strain led to a significant growth defect in DM25 supplemented with acetate (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on growth curves of ancestral strain with gltA1 shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Adding gltA1 on its own to the ancestral REL606 strain led to a significant growth defect in DM25 supplemented with acetate.
source: Other mutations present in these evolved clones are required for gltA1 to have these beneficial effects, as we found that adding gltA1 on its own to the ancestral REL606 strain led to a significant growth defect in DM25 supplemented with acetate (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was beneficial in the genetic background and nutrient context in which it evolved, specifically because it improved acetate utilization.
source: Altogether, these competition results suggest that the gltA1 mutation was beneficial in the genetic background and nutrient context in which it evolved, specifically because it improved acetate utilization.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results of fitness assays in different genetic backgrounds and media conditions.

claim: IclR is a negative regulator of the aceBAK operon.
source: IclR is a negative regulator of the aceBAK operon (Cortay et al., 1991; Maloy and Nunn, 1982), which encodes enzymes for the bypass segment of the glyoxylate pathway (Kornberg, 1966).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The aceBAK operon encodes enzymes for the bypass segment of the glyoxylate pathway.
source: IclR is a negative regulator of the aceBAK operon (Cortay et al., 1991; Maloy and Nunn, 1982), which encodes enzymes for the bypass segment of the glyoxylate pathway (Kornberg, 1966).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Derepression of the aceBAK operon has been shown to increase acetate utilization.
source: Derepression of this operon has been shown to increase acetate utilization (Maloy and Nunn, 1981), reduce acetate excretion (Farmer and Liao, 1997), and decrease lag time when switching from glucose to acetate in mixed media (Spencer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Derepression of the aceBAK operon has been shown to reduce acetate excretion.
source: Derepression of this operon has been shown to increase acetate utilization (Maloy and Nunn, 1981), reduce acetate excretion (Farmer and Liao, 1997), and decrease lag time when switching from glucose to acetate in mixed media (Spencer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Derepression of the aceBAK operon has been shown to decrease lag time when switching from glucose to acetate in mixed media.
source: Derepression of this operon has been shown to increase acetate utilization (Maloy and Nunn, 1981), reduce acetate excretion (Farmer and Liao, 1997), and decrease lag time when switching from glucose to acetate in mixed media (Spencer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: ArcB is the sensor kinase of the ArcAB two-component system.
source: ArcB is the sensor kinase of the ArcAB two-component system, which negatively regulates the expression of genes encoding enzymes in the TCA and glyoxylate cycles, including gltA and the aceBAK operon (Iuchi and Lin, 1988; Waegeman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The ArcAB two-component system negatively regulates the expression of genes encoding enzymes in the TCA and glyoxylate cycles, including gltA and the aceBAK operon.
source: ArcB is the sensor kinase of the ArcAB two-component system, which negatively regulates the expression of genes encoding enzymes in the TCA and glyoxylate cycles, including gltA and the aceBAK operon (Iuchi and Lin, 1988; Waegeman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Introduction of iclR and arcB mutations into the LTEE ancestor strain REL607 greatly increased its proficiency for acetate assimilation.
source: Introduction of these mutations into the LTEE ancestor strain REL607 greatly increased its proficiency for acetate assimilation, as judged by growth curves (Figure 3).
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The evolved iclR and arcB alleles are likely loss-of-function mutations that derepress expression of enzymes needed for acetate assimilation.
source: Therefore, it seems likely that both the evolved iclR and arcB alleles are loss-of-function mutations that derepress expression of enzymes needed for acetate assimilation.
evidence: This is inferred from the known regulatory roles of these genes and the observed growth phenotypes.

claim: The presence of the citT duplication had little effect on the growth of the Cit+/Cit– strain pair containing the gltA1 allele.
source: The presence of the citT duplication had little effect on the growth of the Cit+ /Cit– strain pair containing the gltA1 allele (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The citT mutation greatly prolonged the lag phase before exponential growth in the pair of strains with the gltAwt allele.
source: In stark contrast, the citT mutation greatly prolonged the lag phase before exponential growth in the pair of strains with the gltAwt allele (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on growth curve data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The citT mutation was approximately neutral with respect to fitness in the gltA1 strain background.
source: Co-culture competition experiments between each pair of Cit+/Cit– strains confirmed that whereas the citT mutation was approximately neutral with respect to fitness in the gltA1 strain background, it was highly deleterious in the gltAwt background (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on competition assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The citT mutation was highly deleterious to fitness in the gltAwt background.
source: Co-culture competition experiments between each pair of Cit+/Cit– strains confirmed that whereas the citT mutation was approximately neutral with respect to fitness in the gltA1 strain background, it was highly deleterious in the gltAwt background (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on competition assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was quantitatively necessary for potentiating the evolution of citrate utilization in the LTEE population.
source: We conclude that the gltA1 mutation was quantitatively necessary for potentiating the evolution of citrate utilization in the LTEE population.
evidence: This is concluded from the fitness experiments showing epistatic interactions between gltA1 and citT.

claim: Epistatic interactions between gltA1 and the citT mutation prevented a massive fitness defect that would have led to rapid extinction of newly evolved Cit+ cells.
source: Epistatic interactions between gltA1 and the citT mutation in this evolved genetic background prevented a massive fitness defect that would have almost certainly led to the rapid extinction of any newly evolved Cit+ cells before this rudimentary trait could be refined to the advantageous Cit++ phenotype by further mutations.
evidence: This is inferred from the fitness data showing the deleterious effect of citT without gltA1.

claim: The gltA1 mutation had no effect on gltA transcript levels.
source: We found that gltA1 had no effect on transcript levels in this near-ancestral genetic background.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR measurements shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The gltA2-R mutation reduced gltA mRNA levels by approximately tenfold.
source: In contrast, addition of the gltA2-R mutation reduced gltA mRNA levels by approximately tenfold, whether or not the gltA1 mutation was also present.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The gltA2-R mutation targets the gltA promoter.
source: We conclude that the gltA2-R mutation targets the gltA promoter, and that the fitness effects of this mutation result from reduced gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the location of the mutation and its effect on mRNA levels.

claim: The fitness effects of the gltA2-R mutation result from reduced gene expression.
source: We conclude that the gltA2-R mutation targets the gltA promoter, and that the fitness effects of this mutation result from reduced gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between reduced mRNA levels and fitness effects.

claim: The A258T substitution (gltA1) did not significantly alter the kinetic parameters of citrate synthase.
source: We found that the A258T substitution did not significantly alter the kinetic parameters of the enzyme (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on enzyme kinetics measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: The A162V substitution (gltA2-7) increased the Km values for oxaloacetate and acetyl-CoA.
source: Specifically, the A162V substitution increased the Km values for oxaloacetate (OAA) (143.4 ± 11.1 μM vs 84.2 ± 10.4 μM) and acetyl-CoA (AcCoA) (374.1 ± 41.2 μM vs 138.6 ± 17.6 μM), the two substrates of citrate synthase.
evidence: This is based on enzyme kinetics measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: The A124T amino acid substitution (gltA2-4) resulted in an increased Km for acetyl-CoA and a reduction in the kcat value.
source: The A124T amino acid substitution resulted in an increased Km for acetyl-CoA (295.1 ± 52.6 μM vs 138.6 ± 17.6 μM) and a reduction in the kcat value (33.9 ± 2.7 s-1 vs 51.1 ± 2.5 s-1).
evidence: This is based on enzyme kinetics measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: gltA2 mutations reduce citrate synthase activity either by affecting the Michaelis-Menten parameters of the enzyme or by lowering the steady-state level of the gltA transcript.
source: We conclude that gltA2 mutations likely impact cellular metabolism in a similar manner, as they all reduce citrate synthase activity. This reduction is achieved either by affecting the Michaelis-Menten parameters of the enzyme (gltA2-7 and gltA2-4) or by lowering the steady-state level of the gltA transcript, and thus the expression of the protein (gltA2-R).
evidence: This is concluded from the combined enzyme kinetics and mRNA expression data.

claim: E. coli GltA is a type II citrate synthase that is inhibited by NADH.
source: E. coli GltA is a type II citrate synthase that is inhibited by NADH, the primary product of the TCA cycle (Weitzman, 1966a, 1966b; Weitzman and Jones, 1968).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Wild-type GltA exhibits a Kd and a Ki for NADH of approximately 1 μM.
source: Wild-type GltA was found to exhibit a Kd and a Ki for NADH of ∼1 μM (Table 1 and Figure 5), in excellent agreement with earlier reports (Anderson and Duckworth, 1988; Pereira et al., 1994; Stokell et al., 2003).
evidence: This is based on NADH binding and inhibition measurements shown in Table 1 and Figure 5B, and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: The gltA1 (A258T) mutation greatly diminished NADH binding to citrate synthase.
source: However, the gltA1 (A258T) mutation greatly diminished NADH binding, resulting in an inability to saturate the enzyme within the range of detection in the binding assay, which extends up to ∼10 μM NADH (Dickinson, 1970).
evidence: This is based on NADH binding measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: The gltA1 mutant displayed a Ki for NADH that was higher by a factor of approximately 30 relative to wild-type enzyme.
source: Likewise, the gltA1 mutant displayed a Ki for NADH that was higher by a factor of ∼30 relative to wild-type enzyme.
evidence: This is based on NADH inhibition measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: Each gltA2 mutation restored NADH binding and allosteric inhibition, either partially or fully.
source: Each gltA2 mutation restored NADH binding and allosteric inhibition, either partially or fully.
evidence: This is based on NADH binding and inhibition measurements shown in Table 1 and Figure 5B.

claim: GltA containing both the gltA1 and the gltA2-7 mutations (A258T, A162V) displayed near wild-type Kd and Ki values for NADH.
source: Notably, GltA containing both the gltA1 and the gltA2-7 mutations (A258T, A162V) displayed near wild-type Kd and Ki values for NADH (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on NADH binding and inhibition measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: The A258T gltA1 mutation is predicted to reorient the histidine-110 side chain toward the NADH binding pocket, creating an unfavorable steric barrier to NADH binding.
source: The A258T gltA1 mutation is predicted to reorient the histidine-110 side chain toward the binding pocket, presumably creating an unfavorable steric barrier to NADH binding.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulations and structural modeling.

claim: Addition of secondary gltA2 mutations (A162V or A124T) resulted in simulated structures with histidine-110 oriented between the wild-type and gltA1 extremes.
source: Addition of secondary gltA2 mutations (A162V or A124T) resulted in simulated structures with histidine-110 oriented between these two extremes.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Computational docking of NADH to mutant CS structures predicted relative binding energies that were correlated with the experimentally determined NADH binding affinities.
source: Computational docking of NADH to these mutant CS structures predicted relative binding energies that were correlated with the experimentally determined NADH binding affinities (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on computational docking calculations and comparison with experimental data in Table 1.

claim: For growth on glucose, FBA predicts that low citrate synthase flux will limit the rate of biomass accumulation.
source: For growth on glucose, FBA predicts that low citrate synthase flux will limit the rate of biomass accumulation (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on flux balance analysis modeling shown in Figure 7.

claim: When citrate is the sole carbon source, FBA predicts optimal growth when there is no flux through citrate synthase.
source: However, when citrate is the sole carbon source, FBA predicts optimal growth when there is no flux through CS (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on flux balance analysis modeling shown in Figure 7.

claim: Any citrate synthase activity is detrimental when citrate is the sole carbon source because sufficient flux to synthesize glutamate and other compounds from TCA cycle intermediates is already available.
source: In fact, any CS activity is detrimental because sufficient flux to synthesize glutamate (and other compounds) from TCA cycle intermediates is already available.
evidence: This is inferred from the FBA modeling results.

claim: The optimal level of CS activity in Cit++ cells is predicted to be low but not zero.
source: Cit++ cells must balance using both glucose and citrate, so the optimal level of CS activity in these cells is predicted to be low but not zero (Figure 7), consistent with the effects of the gltA2 mutations we studied.
evidence: This is based on FBA modeling for mixed glucose/citrate growth shown in Figure 7.

claim: FBA indicates that optimal growth on acetate occurs when the flux through citrate synthase is approximately 30% higher than the level that is optimal for growth on glucose.
source: FBA indicates that optimal growth on acetate occurs when the flux through citrate synthase is approximately 30% higher than the level that is optimal for growth on glucose (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on FBA modeling shown in Figure 7.

claim: CS is needed for the glyoxylate cycle, the major pathway for acetate assimilation in E. coli.
source: This increase is expected because CS is needed for the glyoxylate cycle, the major pathway for acetate assimilation in E. coli (Kornberg, 1966).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Flux through the bypass portion of the glyoxylate pathway is needed for optimal growth on acetate but not for growth on glucose.
source: Flux through the bypass portion of the glyoxylate pathway, comprised of the isocitrate lyase (aceA) and malate synthase (aceB) reactions, is needed for optimal growth on acetate but not for growth on glucose (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on FBA modeling shown in Figure 6.

claim: Loss of isocitrate lyase (aceA) activity is predicted to be beneficial for growth on citrate.
source: Loss of isocitrate lyase (aceA) activity is predicted to be beneficial for growth on citrate (Figure 6) because it eliminates unnecessary input of acetyl-CoA into the TCA cycle via the glyoxylate shunt.
evidence: This is based on FBA modeling shown in Figure 6.

claim: A nonsense mutation in aceA was present in approximately 15% of the LTEE population at 33,500 generations and approximately 97% at 34,000 generations.
source: We found that a nonsense mutation in aceA was present in ∼15% of the LTEE population in the 33,500-generation sample and ∼97% in the next 34,000-generation sample.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing data tracking mutation frequencies.

claim: Nearly all Cit++ cells had either the aceA, gltA2-1, or gltA2-9 allele at 33,500 generations.
source: Thus, nearly all Cit++ cells had either the aceA, gltA2-1, or gltA2-9 allele at 33,500 generations (Figure 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the metagenomic sequencing data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: By 34,000 generations the aceA mutation had nearly swept to fixation within the Cit++ clade.
source: By 34,000 generations the aceA mutation had nearly swept to fixation within the Cit++ clade and all subsequent gltA2 alleles occurred in that genetic background.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing data.

claim: All subsequent gltA2 alleles after 34,000 generations occurred in the genetic background containing the aceA mutation.
source: By 34,000 generations the aceA mutation had nearly swept to fixation within the Cit++ clade and all subsequent gltA2 alleles occurred in that genetic background.
evidence: This is based on metagenomic sequencing data.

claim: An aceA mutation may be especially necessary to adjust isocitrate lyase flux because Cit++ strains contain mutations in iclR and arcB transcriptional regulators that compromise regulatory mechanisms that would normally repress aceA gene expression.
source: An aceA mutation may be especially necessary to adjust isocitrate lyase flux because, as discussed earlier, these strains already contain mutations in the iclR and arcB transcriptional regulators that appear to compromise the regulatory mechanisms that would normally repress aceA gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the known regulatory roles of iclR and arcB and the presence of these mutations in the evolved strains.

claim: The clade in which Cit+ would eventually evolve had previously evolved a suite of mutations that improved the utilization of acetate.
source: We found evidence that the clade in which Cit+ would eventually evolve had previously evolved a suite of mutations that improved the utilization of acetate.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined genetic and phenotypic data showing mutations in gltA, iclR, and arcB that improve acetate utilization.

claim: This particular mutational trajectory in the glucose-acetate fitness landscape reshaped metabolic fluxes in a way that facilitated the transition to aerobic citrate utilization.
source: We assert that this particular mutational trajectory in the glucose-acetate fitness landscape reshaped metabolic fluxes in a way that facilitated the transition to aerobic citrate utilization.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined experimental and modeling results showing how acetate-adaptive mutations potentiated Cit+ evolution.

claim: Acetate accumulation has been shown to lead to the appearance and co-existence of glucose and acetate specialists in shorter E. coli evolution experiments.
source: Acetate accumulation has previously been shown to reliably lead to the appearance and co-existence of glucose and acetate specialists in shorter E. coli evolution experiments (Herron and Doebeli, 2013; Spencer et al., 2007; Treves et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous evolution experiments.

claim: The lower concentration of glucose in the LTEE appears to have largely favored the success of generalists that incorporate mutations improving growth on both glucose and acetate.
source: Rather than give rise to this type of stable ecological diversification, the much lower concentration of glucose (and therefore acetate) in the LTEE appears to have largely favored the success of generalists that incorporate mutations that improve growth on both substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with other evolution experiments and the observed mutation patterns in the LTEE.

claim: Mutations in iclR and arcB arose in the population that evolved citrate utilization before 25,000 generations.
source: For example, mutations in the transcriptional regulators, iclR and arcB, arose in the population that evolved citrate utilization before 25,000 generations (Blount et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on genome sequencing data from a previous study.

claim: Similar iclR and arcB/arcA mutations are found in acetate specialists in other evolution experiments.
source: Similar iclR and arcB/arcA mutations are found in acetate specialists in other evolution experiments (Herron and Doebeli, 2013; Spencer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other evolution experiments.

claim: Strains isolated at 50,000 generations from all LTEE populations excreted 50% more acetate, on average, than the ancestral strain.
source: Strains isolated at 50,000 generations from all LTEE populations excreted 50% more acetate, on average, than the ancestral strain (Harcombe et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Mutations in both iclR and arcB are present by 15,000 generations in a population that has not evolved Cit+.
source: Mutations in both iclR and arcB are also present by 15,000 generations in a population that has not evolved Cit+ (Barrick et al., 2009), and arcB/arcA mutations have been found in 11/12 of the LTEE populations (Plucain et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous genomic studies of LTEE populations.

claim: arcB/arcA mutations have been found in 11/12 of the LTEE populations.
source: Mutations in both iclR and arcB are also present by 15,000 generations in a population that has not evolved Cit+ (Barrick et al., 2009), and arcB/arcA mutations have been found in 11/12 of the LTEE populations (Plucain et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: There was universal improvement in acetate growth for 20,000-generation isolates from all LTEE populations.
source: As expected from the widespread appearance of mutations in iclR and arcB/arcA, there was universal improvement in acetate growth for 20,000-generation isolates from all LTEE populations (Leiby and Marx, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Mutations in gltA are rare in the LTEE.
source: In contrast, mutations in gltA are rare in the LTEE.
evidence: This is based on comparison with the frequency of other mutations across LTEE populations.

claim: Only one mutation in citrate synthase was found among 16 clones isolated at generations 20,000 to 40,000 from 7 other LTEE populations.
source: Only one mutation in citrate synthase was found among 16 clones isolated at generations 20,000 to 40,000 from 7 other LTEE populations (Wielgoss et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous genomic study.

claim: Flux through CS is highly regulated in wild-type E. coli, both at the level of transcription and via allosteric feedback inhibition by NADH.
source: Flux through CS is highly regulated in wild-type E. coli, both at the level of transcription (Gosset et al., 2004; Iuchi and Lin, 1988; Park et al., 1994) and via allosteric feedback inhibition by NADH (Weitzman, 1966a, 1966b), as is typical of gram-negative bacteria (Maurus et al., 2003; Weitzman and Jones, 1968).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The initial gltA1 mutation disrupted allosteric repression of CS by NADH.
source: The initial gltA1 mutation in the population that evolved Cit+ disrupted allosteric repression of CS by NADH (Figure 9).
evidence: This is based on NADH binding and inhibition measurements.

claim: Increasing CS activity by disrupting NADH inhibition is predicted to improve E. coli growth on acetate.
source: Increasing CS activity in this way is predicted to improve E. coli growth on acetate.
evidence: This is based on FBA modeling predictions.

claim: The lineage with gltA1 may have had a frequency-dependent fitness advantage when rare against other competitors in the population.
source: As the lineage with gltA1 seems to have come close to extinction in the Ara–3 population before it evolved efficient citrate utilization, it is possible that specializing towards better acetate utilization gave this lineage a frequency-dependent fitness advantage when rare against other competitors in this population that helped preserve it until Cit++ evolved.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed allele dynamics and fitness effects.

claim: An allosterically deregulated citrate synthase enzyme coupled with transcriptional derepression of the TCA and glyoxylate cycles could replenish the intracellular supply of C4-dicarboxylates that are excreted in exchange for citrate by the CitT antiporter.
source: An allosterically deregulated citrate synthase enzyme, which continuously inputs increased carbon flux into the TCA cycle during growth on glucose/acetate, coupled with overall transcriptional derepression of the TCA and glyoxylate cycles, could replenish the intracellular supply of succinate and/or other C4-dicarboxylates that are excreted in exchange for citrate by the CitT antiporter.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the known function of CitT and the metabolic effects of the mutations.

claim: The unbalanced loss of C4-dicarboxylates might explain the detrimental fitness effect of becoming Cit+ via the citT mutation in cells lacking gltA1.
source: The unbalanced loss of these important biosynthetic precursors might explain the detrimental fitness effect of becoming Cit+ via the citT mutation in cells lacking gltA1 (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the observed fitness effects.

claim: The gltA1 mutation was necessary for potentiating the evolution of Cit+ because it converted the citT duplication from a prohibitive step downward into a valley in the fitness landscape into a step in an upward mutational route.
source: Thus, the gltA1 mutation was necessary for potentiating the evolution of Cit+ because it converted the citT duplication from a prohibitive step downward into a valley in the fitness landscape into a step in an upward mutational route.
evidence: This is concluded from the fitness experiments showing epistatic interactions.

claim: When growing on citrate as a carbon source, the CS reaction is expected to be detrimental in that it consumes acetyl-CoA and diverts OAA needed for gluconeogenesis back into the TCA cycle.
source: When growing on citrate as a carbon source, the CS reaction is expected to be detrimental in that it consumes acetyl-CoA and diverts OAA that is needed for gluconeogenesis back into the TCA cycle, a futile-cycle under these conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from metabolic modeling and knowledge of E. coli metabolism.

claim: Allosteric regulation of wild-type CS may not have been able to adjust flux through this reaction to the very low levels that are optimal when growing on citrate with the gltA1 mutation already present.
source: While allosteric regulation of wild-type CS may have been able to adjust flux through this reaction to the very low levels that are optimal under these conditions, this was apparently not possible with the gltA1 mutation already present.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that gltA2 mutations evolved to reduce CS activity in the gltA1 background.

claim: gltA2 mutations emerged that reverse the change in enzyme activity caused by gltA1, either by decreasing mRNA expression levels, by reducing the catalytic proficiency of the enzyme, and/or by restoring allosteric inhibition by NADH.
source: Therefore, gltA2 mutations emerged that reverse the change in enzyme activity caused by gltA1, either by decreasing mRNA expression levels, by reducing the catalytic proficiency of this enzyme, and/or by restoring allosteric inhibition by NADH (Figure 9).
evidence: This is based on the combined molecular characterization of gltA2 mutations.

claim: The LTEE population evolved through three metabolic epochs: first, glucose utilization was optimized; second, acetate utilization was optimized; third, citrate utilization was discovered and optimized.
source: To a first approximation, this LTEE population can be thought of as having evolved through three metabolic epochs: first, glucose utilization was optimized, leading to greater acetate accumulation; second, acetate utilization was optimized in conjunction with further improvements in glucose growth; third, citrate utilization was discovered and optimized.
evidence: This is a conceptual summary of the evolutionary trajectory inferred from the data.

claim: Rudimentary citrate utilization via activation of the citT gene could presumably have arisen at any time and in any of the LTEE populations.
source: While rudimentary citrate utilization via activation of the citT gene could presumably have arisen at any time and in any of the LTEE populations, we have shown that it would have been at a selective disadvantage if it appeared in a non-potentiated genetic background.
evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism of citT activation and the fitness experiments.

claim: If the structure of metabolic and regulatory networks yielded relatively few genetic pathways to improve growth on glucose, it is unlikely that the multi-step mutational pathway to Cit+ requiring mutations that improve acetate utilization would ever have been realized.
source: Moreover, if the structure of the metabolic and regulatory networks and their component genes yielded relatively few genetic pathways with which to improve growth on glucose, it is unlikely that the multi-step mutational pathway to Cit+ that first required mutations that improve acetate utilization would ever have been realized.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed evolutionary trajectory and constraints.

claim: Complexity in both the resource environment and in the genetic architecture of the cell conspired to make the Cit+ metabolic innovation possible.
source: Therefore, complexity in both the resource environment and in the genetic architecture of the cell conspired to make this metabolic innovation possible.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined analysis of the evolutionary trajectory and constraints.

claim: Evolutionary innovations may rely on the inherent malleability of core cellular processes.
source: More broadly, our results demonstrate that evolutionary innovations may rely not only on the acquisition of novel genes or the co-option of molecular machinery for entirely new purposes, but also on the inherent malleability of core cellular processes.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the specific findings of this study.

claim: Metabolic, regulatory, and developmental networks can be dynamically reorganized toward new purposes by only a few mutations in key enzymes and regulatory proteins.
source: Yet, these networks are also poised such that they can be dynamically reorganized toward new purposes by only a few mutations in key enzymes and regulatory proteins.
evidence: This is a general principle illustrated by the gltA mutations and their effects.

claim: It may often be the case that evolution must fine-tune essential links in cellular networks as it traverses epistatic turns and switchbacks on mutational paths leading to successful colonization of new niches.
source: As we observed for changes in citrate synthase activity at different stages in the emergence of citrate utilization during the Lenski LTEE, it may often be case that evolution must fine-tune essential links in these networks as it traverses epistatic turns and switchbacks on the tenuous mutational paths that lead to the successful colonization of new niches.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the specific evolutionary trajectory observed in this study.

claim: CS catalyzes the first irreversible step in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle: the aldol condensation of oxaloacetate (OAA) and acetyl-CoA to form citrate.
source: CS catalyzes the first irreversible step in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle: the aldol condensation of oxaloacetate (OAA) and acetyl-CoA to form citrate.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge.
